The following is a well-known result of Delsarte, Goethals, and Seidel [11] (as discussed in [8, Section 10]), proved using the theory of equiangular lines.



Theorem 1.1 ([11] cf. [32, 8]).



Let GG be a regular graph of order nn with least eigenvalue λ\lambda. If λ<−1\lambda<-1 and multiplicity of λ\lambda is n−kn-k for some k≥1k\geq 1, then n≤k⁡(k+1)2−1n\leq\frac{k(k+1)}{2}-1.





Theorem 1.1 was later generalized by Bell and Rowlinson [6] using the technique of star complements.



Theorem 1.2 ([6]).



Let λ\lambda be an eigenvalue of a graph GG with multiplicity n−kn-k for some positive integer kk. Then either λ∈{0,−1}\lambda\in\{0,-1\} or n≤k⁡(k+1)2n\leq\frac{k(k+1)}{2}. Furthermore, if GG is regular, then n≤(k−1)​(k+2)2n\leq\frac{(k-1)(k+2)}{2}.

The problem of upper-bounding the order of a graph in terms of some graph invariant involving inertia has received attention in the literature. Note that by adding isolated vertices or twins to a graph, one can increase its order without changing its (positive and negative) inertia (see Lemma 3.2). So the problem is meaningful only for reduced graphs.




Motivated by their interest in the connection between the chromatic number and the rank of a graph, the problem of bounding the order of a graph in terms of the rank was first studied by Kotlov and Lovász [24]. They proved that there is a constant c>0c>0 such that any reduced graph with rank rr has order at most c​2r/2c2^{r/2}. Akbari, Cameron, and Khosrovshahi [1] later proposed the following.



Conjecture 2.1 ([1]).



For r≥2r\geq 2, the order of any reduced graph of rank rr is at most m⁡(r)m(r), where




m⁡(r)={2(r+2)/2−2 if ​r​ is even,5⋅2(r−3)/2−2 if ​r​ is odd.m(r)=\begin{cases}2^{(r+2)/2}-2\quad\quad\,\text{ if }r\text{ is even},\\
5\cdot 2^{(r-3)/2}-2\quad\text{ if }r\text{ is odd}.\end{cases}







In [1], the authors also provide constructions of graphs for which the bounds in the above conjecture are tight. Ghorbani, Mohammadian, and Tayfeh-Rezaie [20] proved that if Conjecture 2.1 is false, then a counterexample must exist with rank at most 4646. They also showed that every reduced graph of rank rr has at most 8​m​(r)+148m(r)+14 vertices.
